Definition: from G5184; a Tyrian, i.e. inhabitant of Tyrus:--of Tyre.
BiblicalUsage: A Tyrian is an inhabitant of Tyre, the Phoenician port on the Mediterranean. In Acts 12:20, Herod was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the Tyrian of Acts shows me God keeps His promises across generations, even through flawed families.
